query_text: As a pirate captain, what would you say to your crew to motivate them to search for hidden treasure?

parts.text:
*(The captain steps onto the quarterdeck, resting one hand on the hilt of their cutlass, looking down at the weary, salt-crusted faces of the crew gathered on the main deck. The wind howls slightly through the rigging.)*

"Gather 'round, ye scoundrels! Bring it in and lend me your ears!

I look at ye now, and what do I see? I see men and women who’ve tasted the bitter brine of the sea for months on end. I see hands calloused by rope, faces burned by the sun, and bellies that have gone far too long on hardtack and watered-down grog. I know ye are tired. I know some of ye have started to whisper in the dark, wondering if we’re just chasing ghosts and starlight.

But look at me. Look into my eyes and tell me if you see a captain who has ever led ye to ruin! 

*(The captain pulls out a weathered, yellowed parchment, holding it high so the moonlight catches the ink)*

We hold in our hands not just a map, but the keys to a life none of us were ever promised. Down in the dark, buried beneath the black sands of Dead Man’s Reef, lies the hoard of the Spanish Galleon *San Jose*. 

We’re not talking about a few measly silver reales, lads. We’re talking chests of gold doubloons so heavy they'll make the ship creak! Rubies the size of a coxswain's fist! Emeralds that shine brighter than the northern star! 

Think on it. What awaits us if we turn back? A return to the docks? To be hunted like dogs by the King's men, or to rot in some damp tavern, penniless and forgotten? 

No. Not this crew. Not the finest devils to ever sail under the black flag! 

On that island, we don't just find gold. We find *freedom*. The kind of wealth that buys a man his own land, his own estate, and the respect of those who used to spit on us. We will buy our way into the history books! Every king and governor from here to the Old World will speak our names in whispers of envy and awe!

Aye, the journey ahead is treacherous. The reef is sharp as a cutlass, and they say the island is guarded by the spirits of those who died digging the pit. But I ask ye: since when does a little danger frighten the wolves of the sea? Since when do we bow to ghosts? *We* are the terror of the tide! 

So, what say ye, me hearties? Shall we let the gold rot in the dirt, or shall we tear it from the earth and make it ours?!

Are ye ready to sweat? Are ye ready to fight? Are ye ready to be richer than the lords who banished us to the sea?!

Then man the capstan! Hoist the mainsail! Let the wind catch our sails and carry us to glory! To the treasure, ye beautiful bastards—or to a glorious death in the tryin'! 

**To fortune!**"
